title: taraxacum officinale subsp. laceratum
intro: Taraxacum officinale subsp. laceratum, commonly known as the laciniated dandelion, is a subspecies of the dandelion plant, characterized by its distinctive, deeply cut leaves. The laciniated dandelion has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its ability to support liver health, act as a diuretic, and reduce inflammation. The therapeutic actions of this plant are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and terpenoids, that exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The laciniated dandelion has been traditionally used to treat conditions such as liver and gallbladder disorders, digestive issues, and skin problems.
